Novoselytsya Jewish Cemetery (Austrian side)

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Novoselytsya's Jewish community was historically divided by the Rakitna River into two distinct communities, reflecting the Austro-Russian imperial border that once ran through the town — this is the cemetery of the 'Austrian side' community, its companion documented elsewhere in this collection. In 1917, the Zionist organization Magen Avraam was founded here, eventually drawing more than 500 young members; the first Zionist youth group from Novoselytsya was sent to Eretz Israel in September 1921. The Jewish population reached an extraordinary 86.1 percent of the town by 1930. On July 7, 1941, the day of the German-Romanian occupation, a pogrom claimed 975 lives and burned more than half the town's Jewish houses.
